interpretation: Gentler editing did NOT reduce collateral drift as hoped. IFE (untargeted) FA moved MORE at the gentle setting (0.839->0.911) than the original 25-layer edit (0.839->0.893), despite touching fewer layers at lower rank. RGU (targeted) FA flipped direction entirely -- dropped below baseline (0.741->0.707) rather than rising like the 25-layer version did (0.741->0.759). One genuine improvement: IFE DEF/EWEF did NOT collapse to 0 this time (stayed near baseline, 0.0163 vs 0.0150), unlike the 25-layer version's total collapse -- so the gentler edit is less destructive to the model's ability to produce a correct retain-consistent answer, even though FA moved just as much or more. Combined with the first-ever non-perfect Restricted-CLMI (0.994 vs 1.0), this suggests layer/rank choice has real, non-monotonic effects on the erasure/collateral-damage tradeoff that aren't yet well understood -- fewer layers isn't simply 'safer.' A proper layer x rank sweep (not just one gentler point) is needed before concluding anything about the optimal operating point.
